title: UK settlement (ILR) explained: what it is, how it differs from citizenship and which route may apply to you
summary: What indefinite leave to remain (ILR) is, what it lets you do and how it differs from British citizenship; an overview of the main settlement routes and qualifying periods (Skilled Worker, partners, long residence, Ancestry, Global Talent, BN(O), refugees and others); common requirements; and the Earned Settlement reform, which is not yet in force.

# UK settlement (ILR) explained: what it is, how it differs from citizenship and which route may apply to you

Last updated: 2026-11-21

> **Original overview checked 15 November 2026. Absences and Earned Settlement checked 21 November 2026.** This Guide uses the Immigration Rules and official sources for those respective checks. The Immigration Rules change often, and **which version of the rules applies to your application depends on the rules' own commencement dates and transitional provisions**, so check GOV.UK again before you apply.
>
> This is general information. **It is not legal advice and has not been reviewed by a lawyer.** Meeting any one requirement mentioned here does not mean an application will be granted. If your situation is complicated (for example, a previous refusal, overstaying or a criminal record, long absences from the UK, or a gap in your immigration status), please consult an immigration adviser or lawyer registered with the Immigration Advice Authority (IAA).

Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR, also called "settlement") is an **immigration status** in the UK: once you have it, there is **no longer any time limit** on your stay. Many people think "living here for a number of years" is the only condition, but in fact **each visa route has its own settlement rules**, and the qualifying period, income, English and the way absences are counted can all differ. [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-route-specific)

This Guide first explains what ILR is and how it differs from citizenship, then lists the main routes so you can find the Guide you need.

## 1. Who this Guide is for

- People on a UK visa who are planning for settlement;
- People who are not sure whether, or when, their visa can lead to ILR;
- People who want to understand the difference between ILR and British nationality.

The EU Settlement Scheme ("settled status") for EU, EEA and Swiss citizens and their family members is a separate scheme; section 5 below explains it briefly.

## 2. What ILR lets you do

- **No time limit on your stay**, so you no longer need to extend your visa; [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-rights-no-limit)
- **Work and study freely**: in any business, profession or job, including self-employment, as long as you follow the rules that apply to that work; [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-rights-work-study)
- You can apply for benefits if you are eligible, and healthcare is generally free under the NHS; [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-rights-benefits-nhs)
- **Children born in the UK while you are settled are normally British citizens at birth**; [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-rights-children)
- ILR is the usual first step towards citizenship, but citizenship needs a separate application (see section 3). [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-rights-citizenship)

## 3. How ILR differs from British citizenship

| | ILR | British citizen |
|---|---|---|
| Nature | Immigration status | Nationality |
| Continuous absence from the UK, Channel Islands and Isle of Man | ILR normally lapses after **more than 2 years** continuously outside the UK (EUSS settled status: more than 5 years, or more than 4 for people granted Appendix EU leave as a Swiss national or their family member) | The ILR lapse rules do not apply |
| Can it be taken away? | ILR can be invalidated or revoked, for example on deportation or if it was obtained by deception | Deprivation of nationality is governed by separate law and is outside this Guide |
| Application fee (fee table of 8 October 2026) | £3,226 | Naturalisation £1,709 plus a £130 citizenship ceremony fee |

[See the official basis](#guide-evidence-ilr-vs-citizenship) [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-fees)

**Getting ILR does not make you a British citizen automatically.** Citizenship has its own residence period, absence limits and good character, English and Life in the UK Test requirements; see "Applying for British citizenship after ILR".

## 4. ILR is not granted automatically after a number of years

- **You must apply**, and meet the rules that apply to your application;
- **Time on different routes cannot always be added together.** For example, time spent in the UK as a dependant does not count towards the 5 years required on the Skilled Worker route; [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-sw-qualifying)
- Student and Graduate visas do not lead to settlement themselves; at present that time can only count towards the 10-year long residence route. [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-long-residence)

## 5. The main routes at a glance

This table is only an index. **Every route has other requirements**, so read the relevant Guide or the rules themselves.

| Route | Usual qualifying period under the current rules | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| Skilled Worker | 5 years | Appendix Skilled Worker |
| Spouse or partner (5-year route) | 60 months' continuous residence with partner permission | Appendix FM |
| Spouse or partner (10-year route) | 10 years | Appendix Settlement Family Life |
| Long residence | 10 years' lawful, continuous residence | Appendix Long Residence |
| UK Ancestry | 5 years | Appendix UK Ancestry |
| Global Talent | 3 or 5 years | Appendix Global Talent |
| Innovator Founder | 3 years | Appendix Innovator Founder |
| Hong Kong BN(O) | 5 years | Appendix Hong Kong BN(O) |
| Refugees and humanitarian protection | 5 years (different for asylum claims made on or after 2 March 2026) | Appendix Settlement Protection |
| Private life | 5 or 10 years depending on circumstances | Appendix Private Life |
| EU Settlement Scheme | Usually 5 years' continuous residence | Appendix EU |

[See the official basis](#guide-evidence-table-sw) [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-table-partner) [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-long-residence) [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-table-other-work) [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-table-bno) [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-table-protection) [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-table-private-life) [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-table-euss)

For each route, see "Skilled Worker settlement (ILR): the current 5-year rules and announced reforms", "Settlement for spouses and partners: the 5-year and 10-year routes", "Settlement on the 10-year long residence route" and "Other settlement routes: UK Ancestry, Global Talent, Innovator Founder, BN(O), EUSS, refugees and private life".

## Who the lapse rules cover

Check the legal basis of your grant. The statutory limits are measured in continuous time outside the UK, the Channel Islands and the Isle of Man. Articles 13A to 13C exclude certain overseas postings or time accompanying people on those postings, including specified Armed Forces, Crown service and permanent British Council posts. The exception depends on your grant and circumstances. [Statutory lapse rules](#guide-evidence-lapse-order) · [Home Office EUSS status and absences](#guide-evidence-euss-lapse-official)

Pre-settled status is limited leave. Its automatic lapse, any cancellation, and the qualifying residence needed to move to settled status are separate questions. Check Appendix EU before assuming that the time you spent away will count towards an application. [Appendix EU qualifying residence](#guide-evidence-euss-application)

## 6. Requirements that apply on almost every route

1. **You must be in the UK on the date you apply**, use the correct online form, pay the fee and give your biometrics when required; [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-common-validity)
2. **Suitability** (Part Suitability): for example, criminal records, deception or debts to the NHS or the Home Office can lead to refusal; you generally **must not be an overstayer or on immigration bail** when you apply; [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-common-suitability)
3. **Continuous residence**: many routes, including Skilled Worker, long residence and UK Ancestry, require that you have **not been outside the UK for more than 180 days in any 12-month period** during the qualifying period; the 5-year partner route has different rules. See "Continuous residence and absences: how they are counted for settlement"; [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-common-cr)
4. **English and the Life in the UK Test**: most routes require B1 in speaking and listening, and **for applications made on or after 26 March 2027 most routes rise to B2**; however, the current rules for the Hong Kong BN(O) route still say B1. See "English language and the Life in the UK Test for settlement". [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-common-english)

## 7. The rules are changing: Earned Settlement

On 2 November 2026 the government announced the "Earned Settlement" reform, which would raise the usual qualifying period from 5 to 10 years. **As of 21 November 2026, the general Earned Settlement framework was published as policy. Its detailed Immigration Rules and commencement were still pending**; the table above still shows the current rules. For what the reform says and what remains uncertain, see "Earned Settlement reform tracker: current rules compared with the proposals". [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-es-not-in-force)

## 8. Common misunderstandings

- **"ILR is the same as British nationality."** No. ILR is an immigration status that can lapse after a long absence; citizenship needs a separate application. [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-ilr-vs-citizenship)
- **"Any visa leads to ILR after 5 years."** No. The qualifying period and requirements depend on the route, and Student and Graduate visas do not lead to settlement themselves. [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-long-residence)
- **"EUSS settled status is exactly the same as ordinary ILR."** Both give indefinite leave, but the rules differ: for example, EUSS settled status usually lapses after more than 5 years' continuous absence, or more than 4 for people granted Appendix EU leave as a Swiss national or their family member, while ordinary ILR generally lapses after more than 2 years. [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-ilr-vs-citizenship)
- **"The reform has already started."** The general framework had not come into force as of 21 November 2026. [See the official basis](#guide-evidence-es-not-in-force)

## 9. Checklist

- Confirm which route your current visa belongs to, and what your most recent grant was;
- Work out, for your route, the date you can apply and your days outside the UK;
- Prepare your English evidence and the Life in the UK Test early, and note the B2 change on 26 March 2027;
- Budget for the £3,226 application fee (per applicant);
- Follow the formal rules for Earned Settlement when they are published.

## Related Guides

- "Applying for settlement: when to apply, fees, waiting times and refusals"
- "What documents to prepare for a settlement application"
- "How children and dependants apply for settlement"
- "After you get ILR: rights, eVisa proof of status, travel and losing ILR"
- "Applying for British citizenship after ILR"

---

This is general information and has not been reviewed by a lawyer; if the rules change, GOV.UK and the Immigration Rules take precedence.
